card.summary_ko: 선조 26년(1593, 음력) 정월 6~9일 『선조실록』의 기사. 명 관원들의 도착과 군량 문제, 이여송의 진군, 평양 수복의 승전보와 임금의 사례를 담고, 그해 가을의 명 측 요구와 마찰을 다룬 기사 다섯 건을 덧붙였다.
card.summary_en: Entries from the Seonjo sillok for the 6th-9th days of the first lunar month of 1593: Ming officials arrive, supply troubles, Li Rusong advances, news of the recovery of Pyongyang and the King's thanks; five later entries on Ming demands and friction are added.
card.edition_ko: 中文維基文庫「朝鮮王朝實錄/宣祖實錄/二十六年」(zh.wikisource.org), 판본 2339020, 원전 퍼블릭 도메인 / 전사 CC BY-SA 4.0. 발췌: 정월 6~9일 기사(1월 8일의 인사 기사 등 일부 제외)와 11월·윤11월 기사 5건만 싣고 나머지는 싣지 않음
card.edition_en: Chinese Wikisource, "朝鮮王朝實錄/宣祖實錄/二十六年", revision 2339020; original in the public domain, transcription CC BY-SA 4.0. Excerpt: the entries of the 6th-9th days of the first month (minus a few personnel and unrelated entries) and five entries from the 11th and intercalary 11th months; the rest of the year is not shown

notes.ko:
**저자** 한 사람의 저작이 아니라 국가 기록이다. 원래의 『선조실록』은 1609-1616년 광해군 때 편찬되었는데, 흔히 북인 계열 관료들이 주도했다고 설명한다. 1623년 광해군이 쫓겨난 뒤 서인 중심의 관료들이 이 실록이 자기들에게 불리하게 쓰였다고 보아 『선조수정실록』을 편찬해 1657년에 완성했다. 따라서 두 판본 모두 당파적 시각이 문제가 되며, 이 발췌는 원래의 『선조실록』에서 가져왔다. 선조(1552-1608, 재위 1567-1608)는 글 전체에서 '상(上)'으로 등장한다. 방계 출신으로 처음 왕위에 올랐고 동인과 서인의 분당이 시작된 때 재위했으며 1592년에는 도성을 떠나 피란했다. 그에 대한 역사적 평가는 엇갈린다.

**시대적 맥락** 1592년 일본군이 침입해 한양과 평양을 점령했다. 명은 소규모 병력을 보냈다가 패했고, 이후 명의 사신 심유경이 휴전을 교섭했다. 1592-93년 겨울 송응창 경략 아래 이여송이 이끄는 대군이 조선에 와서 1593년 정월에 평양을 되찾았고, 일본군은 한양 쪽으로 물러났다. 이후 강화 교섭이 이어졌고 1597년에 재침이 일어났다.

**날짜에 대해** 모든 날짜는 음력이다. 선조 26년 정월은 양력으로 대략 1593년 2월에 해당하며, 평양 수복(정월 8일)은 양력 2월 초순에 해당한다. 윤11월은 그해 음력 윤달이다.

**배경** 중문 위키문헌 「宣祖實錄/二十六年」(1593)에서 가져온 발췌로, 정월 6일부터 9일까지의 기사(의주에서의 명 관원 접대와 평양 수복)와, 11월·윤11월의 명 측 요구와 마찰에 관한 기사 다섯 건을 실었다. 인사 이동·날씨 등 주제와 무관한 기사는 뺐다.

**의의** 조선 조정의 입장에서 본 장면으로, 명군에 대한 의존과 군량 수송의 어려움, 명 관원과의 예의와 마찰, 기운을 살펴 승리를 점치는 명 관원의 말, 승전 소식에 대한 기쁨이 나타난다. 11월 기사들은 이후 동맹 관계의 긴장을 보여 준다.

**형식과 주제** 날짜별 궁중 기록이다. 하루가 간지(辛酉, 壬戌 등)로 시작하고, 임금에게 올린 보고(啓)와 임금의 답이 대부분이며, 외교 문서 두 건이 전문으로 실려 있다.

**읽기 도움**
- 啓曰(계왈): 임금에게 아뢰어 말하기를. 馳啓(치계): 급히 달려 보고함.
- 備邊司(비변사): 변방 방어 회의 기구. 政院(정원): 승정원.
- 天兵 / 天將: 명군과 명 장수. 天朝: 명 조정.
- 經略(경략): 송응창. 提督(제독): 이여송.
- 倭(왜): 일본. 捷音(첩음): 승전 소식.
- 移咨 / 回咨(이자 / 회자): 보내는 외교 문서와 그 답.
- 推考(추고): 관원의 잘못을 따져 물음.

번역은 AI가 했고 불확실한 곳은 괄호로 표시했다. '平秀沈'은 명나라 포고문의 인명으로 '平秀次'(도요토미 히데쓰구)의 오기일 가능성이 크나 확실하지 않아 원문대로 두었고, '薜行人'은 '薛行人'(설번)의 오기로 보이며, '沈機'는 인명이 아니라 '속이 깊고 계략이 많다'는 뜻으로 읽었다. '蜍志'는 뜻이 분명하지 않아 번역에 그렇게 밝혔다. 원문에는 따옴표가 어긋난 곳이 있으나 그대로 두었다.
notes.en:
**About the author** The text is a state record rather than the work of one author. The original Veritable Records of King Seonjo were compiled in 1609-1616 under Gwanghaegun by a bureau staffed largely, as usually described, by officials of the Northerner faction (Bukin). After Gwanghaegun's deposition in 1623, Westerner-led officials judged that account biased against them, and a Revised Veritable Records of Seonjo (Seonjo sujeong sillok) was compiled and completed in 1657; so the factional slant of both versions is an issue (the excerpt here comes from the original). Seonjo (1552-1608, r. 1567-1608) speaks throughout as "the King" (sang). He was the first king to come to the throne from a collateral line, ruled when the Eastern-Western factional split began, and fled the capital in 1592; historians' verdicts on him differ.

**Historical context** Japan invaded in 1592 and took Seoul and then Pyongyang. The Ming sent a small force that was defeated, then a Ming envoy, Shen Weijing, negotiated a truce. In the winter of 1592-93 a large army under Li Rusong, with Military Commissioner Song Yingchang above him, came to Korea and in the first lunar month of 1593 recovered Pyongyang. The Japanese then fell back toward Seoul. Later years saw peace talks and a second invasion (1597).

**Dates** All dates are lunar. The first month of Seonjo's 26th year corresponds roughly to February 1593 in the Gregorian calendar, so the recovery of Pyongyang (8th day) falls in early February; the intercalary 11th month is that year's leap month.

**Background** The excerpt is from the Seonjo Veritable Records for the 26th year (1593), taken from Chinese Wikisource. It keeps the entries for the 6th to 9th days of the first lunar month (the Ming officials' arrival at Uiju and the fall of Pyongyang), plus five entries from the 11th and intercalary 11th months on Ming demands and quarrels. Stray entries (appointments, weather) were dropped.

**Significance** It shows the view from the Joseon court: dependence on Ming troops and their logistics, deference and friction with Ming officials, the Ming claim that omens favoured recovery, and joy at the victory. The 11th-month entries show the later strain of the alliance.

**Form and themes** Day-by-day court record. Each day starts with the sexagenary day name (辛酉, 壬戌...). Reports (啓) to the throne and the King's replies make up most of it; two diplomatic notes are quoted in full.

**Reading help**
- 啓曰 (gye-wal): reported to the throne; 馳啓 (chi-gye): reported by express.
- 備邊司 (Bibyeonsa): Border Defence Council; 政院 (Jeongwon): Royal Secretariat.
- 天兵 / 天將: "Celestial troops/generals", i.e. Ming; 天朝: the Ming court.
- 經略 (gyeongnyak): Military Commissioner (Song Yingchang); 提督 (jedok): Commander (Li Rusong).
- 倭 (wae): Japanese; 捷音 (cheop-eum): news of victory.
- 移咨 / 回咨: diplomatic notes sent and answered.
- 推考 (chugo): to question an official for fault.

The translation is by AI; uncertain places are flagged in brackets. 平秀沈, a name in the Ming proclamation, is probably a miscopy of 平秀次 (Toyotomi Hidetsugu) but is left as written; 薜行人 appears to be a miscopy of 薛行人 (Envoy Xue Fan); 沈機 is read as an adjective ('deep in craft') rather than a name; 蜍志 is obscure and flagged as such. Some quotation marks in the source are misplaced and were left untouched.

paragraphs.en: ## First month, 6th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○辛酉，司諫院啓曰：「兵糧輸運事，非不申飭，而州官猶置尋常，略不擧行，極爲駭愕。該曹任其自爲，亦不檢督，不職甚矣。本邑人戶，雖不如舊，而不能調發者，亦是號令不行，色吏用事而然也。請牧使黃璡罷職，鄕所色吏，依軍令決罪，戶曹堂上色郞廳推考，今該曹，各別檢擧，急速施行。」上曰：「幷依啓。牧使推考。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 신유, 사간원계왈: 병량수운사, 비불신칙, 이주관유치심상, 약불거행, 극위해악. 해조임기자위, 역불검독, 부직심의. 본읍인호, 수불여구, 이불능조발자, 역시호령불행, 색리용사이연야. 청목사황진파직, 향소색리, 의군령결죄, 호조당상색랑청추고, 금해조, 각별검거, 급속시행. 상왈: 병의계. 목사추고.
paragraphs.en: On the sinyu day, the Office of Remonstrators reported: "As for the matter of transporting military provisions, it is not that orders were not repeated, but the provincial officials still treat it as ordinary and do not carry it out at all; this is extremely shocking. The board concerned leaves them to do as they please and does not inspect or supervise either; this is a grave neglect of duty. Although the households of this county are not as they were, that nothing can be mobilised is also because orders are not being carried out and the clerks run affairs. We request that Magistrate Hwang Jin be dismissed from office; that the local-office clerks be sentenced according to military law; that the senior officials and the officials in charge of the Board of Revenue be summoned for questioning; and that the board concerned now make special inspections and act with speed." The King said, "All according to the report. Let the magistrate be questioned."

paragraphs.orig: ○是日，兵部主事袁黃渡江。上出迎于龍灣館，又邀劉員外。袁黃曰：「天朝爲貴國發大兵，若到安定絶糧退軍則奈何？」上曰：「各站皆遣官支候，似無不足之憂。恐或軍卒暮到，不及分給也。今聞下敎，當更加申飭。」袁黃曰：「炮車無牛，尙滯途中，大軍雖進，將何爲乎？」上曰：「當更差官督運。」黃裳曰：「前日殿下謂：『倭奴不道，要犯上國，小邦君臣，擧義斥絶，遂觸其怒，先被兇鋒。』云，若倭奴要犯上國，浙江、寧波府等處，亦可來犯，何必由貴國乎？雖欲犯遼、薊，高嶺、靑石嶺之險，其能飛越乎？皇上念屬國被兵，發天兵以救之，且命琉球、暹羅等國，蕩覆倭奴巢穴，貴國但當感恩而已，不當爲此言，戒飭臣僚，不出此言，可也。」上曰：「前日大人有問，寡人不敢不據實以對。今承尊敎，敢不唯命？」劉員外作詩，求和於諸臣。上曰：「此非唱和之時，使勿和答。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 시일, 병부주사원황도강. 상출영우용만관, 우요유원외. 원황왈: 천조위귀국발대병, 약도안정절량퇴군즉내하? 상왈: 각참개견관지후, 사무부족지우. 공혹군졸모도, 불급분급야. 금문하교, 당갱가신칙. 원황왈: 포차무우, 상체도중, 대군수진, 장하위호? 상왈: 당갱차관독운. 황상왈: 전일전하위: 왜노부도, 요범상국, 소방군신, 거의척절, 수촉기로, 선피흉봉. 운, 약왜노요범상국, 절강, 영파부등처, 역가래범, 하필유귀국호? 수욕범료, 계, 고령, 청석령지험, 기능비월호? 황상념속국피병, 발천병이구지, 차명유구, 섬라등국, 탕복왜노소혈, 귀국단당감은이이, 부당위차언, 계칙신료, 불출차언, 가야. 상왈: 전일대인유문, 과인불감불거실이대. 금승존교, 감불유명? 유원외작시, 구화어제신. 상왈: 차비창화지시, 사물화답.
paragraphs.en: On the same day Yuan Huang, Secretary at the Ministry of War, crossed the river. The King went out to greet him at Yongman Lodge and also invited the Supernumerary Secretary Liu. Yuan Huang said, "The Celestial Dynasty is sending a great army for your honoured country; if it reaches Anjeong and, its provisions cut off, has to withdraw, what then?" The King said, "At every station officials have been sent to attend, so there seems to be no worry of shortage. I fear only that if soldiers arrive at dusk it may not be possible to distribute in time. Now that I have heard your instruction, I shall issue stricter orders again." Yuan Huang said, "The cannon-carts have no oxen and are still stuck on the road; even if the main army advances, what will it do?" The King said, "I shall send more officials to supervise the transport." Liu Huangshang said, "The other day Your Highness said: 'The Japanese slaves are lawless and wish to invade the superior state; the ruler and subjects of our small country raised righteous arms and rejected them, and so touched their anger and were the first to suffer their fierce blade.' If the Japanese slaves wished to invade the superior state, they could just as well invade Zhejiang, Ningbo Prefecture and such places; why must they pass through your country? Even if they wished to invade Liao and Ji, could they fly over the dangers of Gaoling and Qingshiling? The Emperor, mindful that a dependent state suffers war, has sent Celestial troops to rescue it, and has also ordered Ryukyu, Siam and other countries to overturn the nests of the Japanese slaves. Your country should simply be grateful; you should not say such things. It would be right to warn your officials not to say them." The King said, "The other day, when the Grandee asked, I could not but answer truthfully. Now that I have received your instruction, how dare I not obey?" Supernumerary Liu composed a poem and sought replies in verse from the officials. The King said, "This is not a time for matching poems; have them not reply."
## First month, 7th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○壬戌，大提學尹根壽啓曰：「臣以庸謬無狀，濫蒙兩朝殊遇，美職淸班，歷遍殆盡，遂躋崇班，分劑旣過，鬼責隨至，三四年來，孩抱中物，化爲糞壤者，前後凡四，情鍾所在，肝肺寸鑿，心神昏錯，撫事輒忘，形骸雖存，已覺奄奄如蜍志。不幸國家有開闢所無之兵禍，扈駕蒼黃，力疾班行。今者柄文之除，乃及於臣，聞命震悸，不知所處。文衡之任，其選最重，自祖宗朝，必擇長於斧藻，望仗一世者授之，未有如臣之匪才而冒據者，貽辱名器，實自臣始，何心能安？臣在先朝，雖猥預賜暇之列，而才不及人，又不自力，詩多拙語艱澁，表箋則素所不解，此則一時流輩，無不知之，非臣之飾說也。加以憂患嬰心，精神瞀亂，如上所云，舊學盡忘，塊然土木。又事非平時，上國文書，絲絡而至，登時回答，專責典文。如臣之空踈昏謬，其何能左酬右應而無滯乎？念非私憂，實係國體，伏望聖慈，曲察微懇，亟收成命，以授其人。」上曰：「可合，勿辭。」再辭，不允。
paragraphs.reading: ○ 임술, 대제학윤근수계왈: 신이용류무상, 남몽양조수우, 미직청반, 역편태진, 수제숭반, 분제기과, 귀책수지, 삼사년래, 해포중물, 화위분양자, 전후범사, 정종소재, 간폐촌착, 심신혼착, 무사첩망, 형해수존, 이각엄엄여서지. 불행국가유개벽소무지병화, 호가창황, 역질반행. 금자병문지제, 내급어신, 문명진계, 부지소처. 문형지임, 기선최중, 자조종조, 필택장어부조, 망장일세자수지, 미유여신지비재이모거자, 이욕명기, 실자신시, 하심능안? 신재선조, 수외예사가지열, 이재불급인, 우부자력, 시다졸어간삽, 표전즉소소불해, 차즉일시유배, 무부지지, 비신지식설야. 가이우환영심, 정신무란, 여상소운, 구학진망, 괴연토목. 우사비평시, 상국문서, 사락이지, 등시회답, 전책전문. 여신지공소혼류, 기하능좌수우응이무체호? 념비사우, 실계국체, 복망성자, 곡찰미간, 극수성명, 이수기인. 상왈: 가합, 물사. 재사, 불윤.
paragraphs.en: On the imsul day, the Grand Academician Yun Geun-su reported: "I, mediocre, blundering and without merit, have excessively received special favour from two reigns; the fine posts and pure ranks I have passed through almost completely, and I have finally risen to a high rank. My portion has already been overfull, and ghostly reproaches follow it. In these three or four years, those who were in my arms as infants have, one after another, four in all, turned into dung and earth; my feelings are fixed where they lie, my liver and lungs are drilled through inch by inch, my mind is muddled, I forget things as I handle them, and though my body remains I already feel myself languishing, barely alive [the phrase 'like a toad's will' is obscure]. Unfortunately the state has met a military calamity unknown since the world's opening; I accompanied the royal carriage in haste and joined the ranks in illness. Now the appointment to the Literary Balance has fallen on me; hearing the order I trembled and did not know what to do. The post of Literary Balance is the most weighty of selections: since the ancestral reigns it has always been given to one skilled in polished composition and looked up to by the whole age, and there has never been one as untalented as I who has usurped it. To bring disgrace on the name and the vessel [of office] begins in truth with me; how could my heart be at ease? Under the former king I was indeed included among those granted study leave, but my talent did not match others, and I did not exert myself either; my poems have many clumsy and obscure lines, and as for memorials and addresses I have never understood them. All my contemporaries know this; it is not my embellished speech. Moreover, with grief and worries entangling my heart, my spirit is confused, as said above; I have forgotten all my former learning and sit like a clod of earth or wood. Again, these are not ordinary times; documents from the superior state arrive one after another like threads on a skein, and one must reply at once, which is the sole responsibility of the one in charge of literature. As empty, slipshod, muddled and mistaken as I am, how could I handle left and right without hindrance? Considering that this is not a private worry but concerns the national body, I humbly hope that Your Majesty's sagely kindness will sympathetically examine my small plea, quickly withdraw the order already given, and confer the post on a suitable person." The King said, "It is fitting; do not decline." He declined again; it was not granted.

paragraphs.orig: ○袁主事，質明，與金相公者，共出聚勝亭岸上，望氣而言曰：「三氣皆旺，而望見國王所在之宮，王氣尤爲旺盛，恢復無疑云。(怪哉！主事望氣之說也。古者，喪國之君，改紀修政，以復舊業者，則有之，未聞由於氣之衰旺也。宜其被左道，惑象之誚也。)○上曰：「劉員外之言，雖是假設之辭，而似爲未安，今遣承旨致辭曰：『倭賊之悖逆，本國之情由，俱載於上年黃叅將齎去倭情書契中，大人若下覽其書，則彼此之情由，自當畢露。昨昨日，大人下間被患之由，不敢不據實以對，而昨承尊敎，不勝惶恐，無路謝罪。願還受所呈之書。』云云，如何？」政院啓曰：「頃者所答之辭，只是據實以對，初非今日創語也。如薜行人、李提督等，非不聞此語，而無此說。臣等妄意，天朝之於小邦，實有唇齒之勢，宜救援而不宜講和也，無乃彼之所見，不能了了於此，乃有此說耶？昨旣隨問暴白，今不須更爲分疏。第事係重大，請令大臣議處。」備邊司啓曰：「臣等伏見，自上立談間，爲答劉員外之言，眞是摭實，少無虛假，今不宜謝還所呈小紙。所謂禮者，不失人，亦不失己之謂也。依政院啓辭，不必致辭於其間，靜以竢之爲得也。」

paragraphs.en: Secretary Yuan, at dawn, together with a certain Minister Kim, went out onto the bank by Chwiseung Pavilion and gazed at the vapours, saying, "The three vapours are all vigorous, and looking toward the palace where the King is, the royal vapour is especially vigorous; recovery is beyond doubt." (Comment of the historian: How strange! The Secretary's talk of gazing at vapours. In antiquity there were rulers who lost their states and then reformed their regulations and mended their government and so recovered their old enterprise, but I have never heard that it came about through the waxing or waning of vapours. No wonder he was reproached as following heterodox arts and being deluded by omens.) The King said, "Supernumerary Liu's words, though hypothetical, seem improper. I shall now send a Royal Secretary to convey this: 'The rebellion of the Japanese bandits and the circumstances of our country were all recorded in the letter on the Japanese situation that Deputy Commander Huang took with him last year. If Your Excellency would look at that document, the circumstances on both sides will naturally be fully revealed. The day before yesterday, when Your Excellency asked about the cause of the calamity we suffered, I could not but answer truthfully; yesterday I received your instruction and am overcome with fear and have no way to apologise. I wish to take back the document that I presented.' What do you think?" The Royal Secretariat reported: "The words answered earlier were only a truthful answer to a question; they were not newly invented today. Such persons as Messenger Xue [the text has 薜, evidently a miscopy of 薛] and Commander Li were not unaware of these words, yet there was no such talk from them. We presume that the Celestial Dynasty and our small country are truly in a relation of lips and teeth, and it should rescue us rather than make peace; perhaps what he sees is not clear on this and so he has this saying? Since yesterday's answer was given to a question and made plain, there is no need now to explain further. But the matter is weighty; we ask that the ministers deliberate and deal with it." The Border Defence Council reported: "We humbly observe that the King's answer to Supernumerary Liu, given while speaking standing, was truly factual, without the least falsehood; it is not appropriate now to apologise and take back the little paper that was submitted. What is called ritual means neither losing others nor losing oneself. According to the Secretariat's statement there is no need to send any words in between; quietly waiting is the right course."

paragraphs.orig: ○司憲府啓曰：「天將，今已進駐安定，而兵器尙未輸運，留置道路，極爲駭愕。請一路尤甚遲滯守令，令各驛監掌軍糧宰臣，兼爲檢察，使轉報朝廷，或送宣傳官，或遣禁府郞廳，一以軍律處斷。」上從之。

paragraphs.en: The Office of the Inspector-General reported: "The Celestial generals have now advanced to Anjeong, but weapons have still not been transported and are left lying on the roads; this is extremely shocking. We request that for those magistrates along the route who are most guilty of delay, the senior ministers in charge of military grain at each post-station also inspect and supervise, and report to the court, and that either royal messengers be sent or officers of the Office of Royal Investigation be dispatched, and that punishment be decided entirely by military law." The King followed the report.

paragraphs.orig: ○禮曹判書尹根壽啓曰：「佟叅將在淸心堂，臣今日進見，則參將與張都司同坐。叅將曰：『李副將如栢，初四日，先到定州東邊，令金子貴哄倭曰：「沈遊擊到此。」行長卽令倭子二十三名出迎。酉時，來到陣中，李如栢斬十五級，擒三名，五倭則逃脫，日已昏黑，雖不知去向，然伏兵斷絶歸路，必不得到平壤，生擒三倭，一則張大膳，一則小將。大膳言：「初五日，衆倭齊出，迎接沈遊擊」云，若如其言，則初五日必大戰，今夜當有報來，否則倭奴必詗知大兵之至，而守城不出矣。且李提督，初欲屯於安定休兵，而初四日作事如彼，不可小緩，想已直進。若倭守城不出，則亦可休息數日而戰。且聞平壤之倭，其數不多，只五六千，而皆選鋒驍勇，城中無鹽醬。金子貴將小刀等物，要換鹽醬，而無從覓得云。且聞關伯平秀吉來駐對馬島，其弟其子皆死，勢甚孤單。且李提督到肅寧，聞密雲軍劉信者，侵擾人家，壓殺小兒，便將劉信斬梟。且令火炮、軍器等物，星火運送，剋復平壤，不在多日，平壤卽復，則休兵數日，前進王京，只恐春氷漸薄，大軍難過大同江，過涉具亦可預備。黃海一路芻糧，可以接濟乎？』臣答以：『黃海大路，賊常往來，芻糧儲於近處，而迤傍州郡，略皆儲峙，以備臨時接濟之用矣。』叅將欣然曰：『然則好矣。』又曰：『宋經略，初六日，發遼東，以日計之，則明日當到鳳鳳城。』云。」

paragraphs.en: Yun Geun-su, Minister of Rites, reported: "Deputy Commander Tong is at Cheongsimdang. When I went in to see him today, the Deputy Commander was sitting with Regional Commandant Zhang. The Deputy Commander said, 'Deputy General Li Rubai, on the fourth day, first arrived at the east of Jeongju and had Jin Zigui deceive the Japanese by saying, "Roving Commander Shen is coming here." Yukinaga at once sent twenty-three Japanese to welcome him. At the hour of the rooster (5-7 p.m.) they arrived in the camp. Li Rubai beheaded fifteen and captured three; five Japanese escaped. Though it was dark and their whereabouts are unknown, ambushes cut off their retreat, so they surely cannot reach Pyongyang. Of the three taken alive, one is Zhang Daxian and one a junior commander. Daxian said, "On the fifth the Japanese all came out together to welcome Roving Commander Shen." If so, there will surely be a great battle on the fifth, and a report should come tonight; if not, the Japanese slaves must have learned that the great army has come and are holding the city without coming out. Besides, Commander Li had at first intended to halt at Anjeong and rest the troops, but given what happened on the fourth, there can be no slight delay, and I suppose he has already advanced straight on. If the Japanese hold the city and do not come out, then we can also rest a few days and fight. I also hear that the Japanese in Pyongyang are not many, only five or six thousand, but all picked, brave vanguard troops, and that there is no salt or sauce in the city. Jin Zigui took small knives and other things hoping to exchange them for salt and sauce, but there was no way to find any. I also hear that the Kanpaku Hideyoshi has come to stay on Tsushima, that his younger brother and his son have both died, and that his position is very isolated. Also, when Commander Li reached Suknyeong, he heard that Liu Xin of the Miyun army was harassing people's homes and had crushed a small child to death, and at once had Liu Xin beheaded and his head displayed. He has also ordered cannon, weapons and the like to be sent forward at breakneck speed. The recovery of Pyongyang will not take many days; once Pyongyang is retaken, we will rest the troops a few days and advance on the royal capital. I fear only that the spring ice is gradually thinning and the great army will find it hard to cross the Daedong River; boats and fording equipment can be prepared in advance. Can the fodder and provisions of the Hwanghae road be used for supply?' I answered, 'On the main road of Hwanghae the bandits constantly come and go, so fodder is stored in nearby places, and the districts along the way have all stored a certain amount in preparation for supply as needed.' The Deputy Commander said gladly, 'If so, good.' He also said, 'Military Commissioner Song set out from Liaodong on the sixth; reckoning by days, tomorrow he should reach Fenghuangcheng [the text has 鳳鳳城, a miscopy].'"

paragraphs.orig: ○大明欽差經略防海禦倭軍務兵部(武庫淸吏司員外郞劉黃裳，職方淸吏司主事袁黃。)移咨曰：爾國素敦文物，世篤忠貞。邇者，倭夷不道，長驅荐食，致君臣越在草莽，瑣尾流離，何其困也？我大明皇帝，念爾二百年來恪守臣節，不惜萬金之費，命將徂征。爾國中，豈無宗戚，受重寄而忠憤薰心，豈無縣官，守地方而慷慨委命，豈無忠臣，懷主憂臣辱之念，豈無義土，萠捐𨈬報國之思？宜乘天威震疊，速招集義兵，各提一旅之師，共申九伐之志。今倭夷逞强，其勢必亡，爾國雖微，其勢必興，試相與籌之。先論天道，朝鮮分野，屬析木之次，上年木星躔寅而日本來侵，是我得歲，而彼侵之，逆天而行，雖强亦弱，一也。倭性畏寒，今歲厥陰，風木司天，陽明燥金，爲初之氣，立春後，尙有二三十日寒氣未消，天時可乘，二也。爾國君臣，俱聚此城，晨起望氣，鬱鬱蔥蔥如練如蓋，旺氣在我，勢必恢復，三也。次論人事，我大國雄兵，如虎如熊，無敵大砲，一發千步，彼不量力，當成虀粉，一也。經略宋、沈機畜謀，神鬼難測，李提督一腔忠義，百戰餘勇，有古名將風，二職，素仗忠貞，同心協贊，誓滅此賊，以報天子，合兩國之師，驅此窮鬼，如振落耳，二也。關伯强暴，上刼制其主，下虐使其衆，天欲亡之，實假手于我，三也。昨見國王，擧動安詳，手姿俊偉，勢必中興，而爾國前所遣諸使，請兵天朝，誠意懇惻，淚下如注，庶幾申包胥泣楚之意，君臣若此，豈終淪困。以順討逆，何功不成，四也。倭奴所恃，唯鳥銃。然三發之後，卽難繼矣，其兵雖衆，强者無幾，但殺其前行一二百人，餘皆望風遁矣，此皆可勝之機，正志士立功之秋也。我朝出令，不論我國爾國，但有人能擒斬平秀吉、平秀沈及僧玄蘇者，每名，賞銀一萬兩，封伯世襲，擒斬平秀家、平秀忠、平行長、平義智、平鎭信等有名諸酋者，每名，賞銀五千兩，世襲指揮使，以下擒獲，各有賞格。爾國臣民，但能乘時紏衆，共立大功，旣可以復本國之社稷，又可以徼天子之厚賞。以衰國之遺黎，爲起家之始祖，豈不暢哉！爲此咨請，須速傳示各道臣民，義兵已起者，便爲前進，未起者速爲招集，或協力以挫其威武，或迭出以分其勢，或邀其惰歸，或斷其餉道，諸所機宜，皆聽自便。○回咨曰：竊恐當職，守藩無狀，劇賊侵逼，宗社丘墟，生靈魚肉，喪地蹙師，寄命一隅。上負天朝，下慙臣民，誠無以自謝於覆幬之間，負非引咎，俯仰蹙縮，伏蒙聖朝天地洪造。曲念先故，刑章不加，寵恤曠古，恩非所望，心悸神慄，日夜扣心飮泣，雖欲少答生成。實難報效，苟度歲月，得及新春者，秋毫皆帝力也。邇者，伏見大軍遠來，飢渴暴露，資糧裝運，人畜顚損，加之諸老爺，勤劬霜雪，不遑啓處，致此其誰？孽由己作，雖欲擧口譚恩，無說可容，一禮效感，無物可稱。向自提督李進軍之後，竊深風霧夙夜之慮，寢固不敢，食豈不咽。頃經略宋檄文一通，辭嚴義正，雷厲風飛，卽蒙二老爺敦諭滿幅。言順理切，春和秋澟，神策淵宏，妙算玄深，通貫天人，出入顯晦，誠所謂明足以儷日月，幽足以動鬼神。敢不星馳一紙，風諭八方，俾人人皷懦而懷勇，感德而怛威也？至於小邦將卒，戰雖戮力，急於自救，而勸勉諄懇，賞班大國，是固踰涯，豈敢承當？二老爺爲下國慮，實勤且加，敝邦，雖甚偏小，亦豈無域內一二忠義，感咨內歷指之意，而知天朝曲遂之德者，其勇其怯，臨戰自現，有罪無罪，悉稟威斷。第念當職，積釁失國，無顔自立，而二位涵容，反賜謬褒，引之於興復，是雖二老爺拂試奬勉，要强人心，而豈復有䏕氣，在當職身上者，倘有之？此實天朝祥氛洋溢，延及屬國，當職豈敢若已有之？依此宣布，神祗謂何，臣民謂何？但咨內事理，不敢輒刪，一依來諭，不勝兢惶忸怩之至。

paragraphs.en:
A diplomatic note was transmitted by the Ming Imperial Commissioner and Military Commissioner for coastal defence against the Japanese, of the Ministry of War (Liu Huangshang, Supernumerary Director of the Bureau of Military Stores; Yuan Huang, Secretary of the Bureau of Operations): "Your country has long been devoted to culture and for generations steadfast in loyalty. Recently the Japanese barbarians, lawless, have advanced in long strides, eating away your land, so that ruler and subjects have been left in the wilds, scattered and wandering. How hard that is! Our Great Ming Emperor, mindful that for two hundred years you have kept your duty as a vassal, has spared no expense of ten thousand pieces of gold and has ordered generals to set out on campaign. Among your people, are there no imperial kinsmen who have received heavy trust and whose hearts are filled with loyal indignation? Are there no county officials who guard their territory and would give their lives with passion? Are there no loyal subjects who feel that when the lord is troubled the subject is shamed? Are there no righteous men who sprout the thought of giving up their lives to repay the country? You should take advantage of the awe of Heaven's might, quickly gather righteous troops, each leading a force, and jointly carry out the will of the nine punitive campaigns. Now the Japanese barbarians are exerting force, but their momentum must lead to ruin; though your country is feeble, its momentum is bound to rise. Let us reckon it together. First on the Way of Heaven: Joseon's sky-division belongs to the Xi Mu stage [Jupiter's station]; last year Jupiter stood in Yin when Japan invaded. That is, we held the year and they invaded against it; going against Heaven, though strong they are weak. This is the first point. The Japanese by nature fear cold; this year the Jueyin wind-wood rules the sky and Yangming dry metal is the first qi; after the beginning of spring there remain twenty or thirty days of unspent cold. Heaven's timing can be used. That is the second. Your ruler and ministers are all gathered in this city; rising in the morning and watching the vapours, they are lush and dense like silk and a canopy. The vigorous vapour is on our side and the momentum must be one of recovery. That is the third.

"Next on human affairs: our great state's mighty troops are like tigers and bears, with invincible great cannon that shoot a thousand paces; the foe, not weighing his own strength, will be ground to mincemeat. That is the first. Military Commissioner Song, deep in craft and stocked with stratagems, is such that gods and ghosts cannot fathom him; Commander Li, with a heart wholly of loyalty and righteousness and courage left from a hundred battles, has the air of the famous generals of old. These two officers (Song and Li), long relying on loyalty, cooperate with one heart, vowing to destroy these bandits and repay the Son of Heaven. With the combined armies of the two countries driving out these wretched ghosts is like shaking down fallen leaves. That is the second. The Kanpaku is violent: above he coerces his lord, below he cruelly uses his people. Heaven wishes to destroy him and in truth lends its hand to us. That is the third. Yesterday I saw the King; his bearing was composed, and his hands and manner handsome and grand; he is bound to restore the state. And the envoys your country sent earlier to ask the Celestial Dynasty for troops were sincere and earnest, their tears falling like pouring rain, much like Shen Baoxu weeping at the Qin court to save Chu. With a ruler and ministers like this, how could you remain sunk in distress in the end? With the obedient attacking the rebellious, what merit will not be achieved? That is the fourth. What the Japanese slaves rely on is only the arquebus; but after three shots it is hard for them to continue. Though their troops are many, the strong are few; if we kill one or two hundred of the front rank, the rest will flee at the sight. All these are chances for victory, precisely the time for men of resolve to establish merit.

"Our court's order is this, regardless of whether it is a person of our country or of yours: whoever can capture or behead Hideyoshi, Hidetsugu [written 平秀沈 in the text; 沈 is probably a copying error for 次] or the monk Gensō will be rewarded, for each one, with ten thousand taels of silver and enfeoffed as an earl with hereditary succession. Whoever captures or beheads such named chiefs as Hideie, Hidetada [as written; the name is uncertain], Yukinaga, Yoshitoshi and Shigenobu will be rewarded with five thousand taels of silver each and the hereditary rank of Commander; for those below that, there is a scale of rewards for each. If the subjects and people of your country only seize the opportunity, rally the multitude and jointly achieve great merit, they can both recover your country's altars of the state and earn the Emperor's generous reward. To make the founding ancestor of a house out of a remnant of the people of a ruined country, how delightful that would be! For this reason we send this note; it must be quickly communicated to the subjects and people of every province: where righteous troops have already risen, let them advance; where they have not, let them quickly be gathered; either cooperate to crush the enemy's might, or sally out in turn to split his force, or intercept him as he returns weary, or cut his supply lines. All expedients are left to your convenience."

A reply note said: "I privately fear that I, the holder of this office, have been unworthy in guarding the frontier; fierce bandits pressed in, the royal shrines and altars have become ruins, the people have been made fish and meat, land has been lost and forces contracted, and I entrust my life to a single corner. Above I have failed the Celestial Dynasty, below I am ashamed before my subjects; truly I have no way to apologise between the covering Heaven and the bearing Earth. I bear the fault and take the blame, bowing and shrinking back at every turn. Humbly I have received the Holy Dynasty's great creation like heaven and earth, which, considering my forebears, applied no penalty; its kindness was unprecedented and beyond what I could hope for. My heart trembles and my spirit shudders; day and night I beat my breast and swallow my tears. Though I wish to repay a little of the giving of life, it is truly hard to repay; that I have passed the months and reached the new spring is, down to the last hair, the Emperor's power. Recently I have seen the great army come from afar, hungry, thirsty and exposed, with supplies and loads hauled until men and beasts fall; moreover the Lords have toiled through frost and snow without leisure to rest. Who caused this? The calamity is of my own making; though I wish to speak of kindness, I have no words that could be accepted; though I wish to offer the courtesy of gratitude, I have nothing that could match it. Since the march of Commander Li I have deeply worried night and day about wind and fog; I cannot sleep, and how could I swallow my food? Not long ago Military Commissioner Song's proclamation, severe in words and proper in meaning, thundering and flying like the wind, and then the two Lords' full-page earnest exhortation, smooth in words and apt in reasons, spring-warm and autumn-chill, with divine strategy so deep and wonderful calculation so profound, penetrating Heaven and man, passing in and out of the manifest and the hidden, can truly be said to be bright enough to match the sun and moon and obscure enough to move ghosts and spirits. How dare I not send by star-speed a single sheet to proclaim it to the eight directions, so that every man will take courage in his weakness and be moved by virtue yet fear awe? As for the generals and soldiers of my small country, though they fight with all their strength, they are in a hurry to save themselves; and the exhortation is earnest, with rewards and ranks bestowed by the Great Country, which exceed what is proper; how would I dare accept them? The two Lords have worried for the lower country, truly diligently and more. Though my country is very small and distant, would there not be one or two loyal and righteous people within our borders who, moved by the intent shown in your note and knowing the Celestial Dynasty's complying virtue, will show whether they are brave or timid on the field of battle? Guilt or innocence will all be left to your authoritative decision. But I, the holder of this office, having accumulated faults and lost my state, have no face to stand; yet you two Lords have tolerated me and instead bestowed mistaken praise, leading me toward the restoration. Although this is the two Lords' encouragement to strengthen people's hearts, how could there be any courageous vapour in my own person? If there were, it would truly be the auspicious air of the Celestial Dynasty overflowing and extending to its vassal country; how would I dare possess it as though it were mine? If it were proclaimed in this way, what would the gods say, and what would my subjects say? But as to the principles and matters in the note, I do not dare to delete them casually; I follow your instruction in full, with a fear and shame I cannot bear.
## First month, 8th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○備邊司啓曰：「京畿左道監司李廷馨，因本處乏糧，將移海邊云。雖有精兵，糧絶則無用。東路一帶，無險可恃，賊勢極熾，無容足之地，此出於不得已之計。而天兵大至，若有長驅直擣之勢，在我不可不登時挾攻，以挫先鋒。廷馨一離其地，節制無人，姑留以待，徐議進退，似爲便當。義兵之弊，論之已熟，前後行移，非一非再。而日益驕橫，使聽監司之令，則不從，使聽禹性傳節制，則亦不從，皆稱無餉，一向渙散云。其不統於邑倅，不從將令者，一以軍法從事。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 비변사계왈: 경기좌도감사이정형, 인본처핍량, 장이해변운. 수유정병, 량절즉무용. 동로일대, 무험가시, 적세극치, 무용족지지, 차출어부득이지계. 이천병대지, 약유장구직도지세, 재아불가부등시협공, 이좌선봉. 정형일리기지, 절제무인, 고류이대, 서의진퇴, 사위편당. 의병지폐, 논지이숙, 전후행이, 비일비재. 이일익교횡, 사청감사지령, 즉부종, 사청우성전절제, 즉역부종, 개칭무향, 일향환산운. 기불통어읍쉬, 부종장령자, 일이군법종사.
paragraphs.en: The Border Defence Council reported: "The Governor of the left side of Gyeonggi, Yi Jeong-hyeong, because his locality is short of grain, is said to be about to move to the seashore. Even with elite troops, if the grain runs out they are useless. In the eastern road region there is no defensible terrain, the enemy's strength is very great, and there is no room to set a foot; so this is a measure of necessity. But the Celestial troops are arriving in force, with the momentum of driving straight in and striking, and on our side we cannot but attack from both flanks at the proper time to blunt the vanguard. If Jeong-hyeong leaves that ground there will be no one to command; for now let him remain there in waiting and discuss advance or retreat at leisure, which seems the suitable course. The ills of the righteous armies have been discussed to exhaustion, and orders have been sent before and after not once or twice, yet they grow daily more arrogant and unruly. If they are told to obey the governor's orders, they do not obey; if they are told to obey the command of U Seong-jeon, they do not obey that either; they all say they have no pay and keep dispersing. Those who are not subordinate to the district magistrate and do not obey the generals' orders should be dealt with entirely by military law."

paragraphs.orig: ○工曹判書韓應寅，漢城府判尹李德馨馳啓曰：「本月初三日，提督自嘉山到安州，初昏招都體察使柳成龍，暫話而罷。約於今日，偕到肅寧館，與都元帥及臣等，更議兵事，提督夜不收一人，回自平壤城中，言：『倭賊，尙不知天兵出來消息。』且聞沈遊擊墜馬傷足，以肩輿登途，欲令倭賊二百餘名，來迎于中路，而倭將使五倭出迎。提督聞此言，傳言臣等曰：『我當速爲前往，分付諸將，許令五倭出迎，仍爲生擒，佯言沈遊擊將至，則倭賊必陳兵出城，因以掩擊，可以取勝』云。提督多般設策，進兵之期，似不出三四日之內，而各樣兵器，裝載車輻，過半落後。臣等在嘉山，令從事官李延慶，催發人牛，及時輸運，而各官未易擧行，方爲悶慮。今到安州，又聞戚遊擊戰車百餘輻，全未運到，更遣從事官李光庭，急急催運以來。大槪今日之憂，只在糧餉一事，而聞肅川所儲米太，甚爲不敷。臣等與都體察使及調度使尹承勳相議，以次移轉隣邑之穀，前到安定，別加撿勑計料。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 공조판서한응인, 한성부판윤이덕형치계왈: 본월초삼일, 제독자가산도안주, 초혼초도체찰사유성룡, 잠화이파. 약어금일, 해도숙녕관, 여도원수급신등, 갱의병사, 제독야불수일인, 회자평양성중, 언: 왜적, 상부지천병출래소식. 차문심유격추마상족, 이견여등도, 욕령왜적이백여명, 내영우중로, 이왜장사오왜출영. 제독문차언, 전언신등왈: 아당속위전왕, 분부제장, 허령오왜출영, 잉위생금, 양언심유격장지, 즉왜적필진병출성, 인이엄격, 가이취승운. 제독다반설책, 진병지기, 사불출삼사일지내, 이각양병기, 장재차복, 과반락후. 신등재가산, 영종사관이연경, 최발인우, 급시수운, 이각관미역거행, 방위민려. 금도안주, 우문척유격전차백여복, 전미운도, 갱견종사관이광정, 급급최운이래. 대개금일지우, 지재량향일사, 이문숙천소저미태, 심위불부. 신등여도체찰사급조도사윤승훈상의, 이차이전인읍지곡, 전도안정, 별가검칙계료.
paragraphs.en: The Minister of Public Works Han Eung-in and the Magistrate of Seoul Yi Deok-hyeong reported by express: "On the third of this month the Commander went from Gasan to Anju and at dusk summoned Chief Inspector Yu Seong-ryong for a brief talk. It was arranged that today he would come with the Commander-in-Chief and us to Suknyeong Lodge to discuss military matters further. The Commander's night scout came back from inside the city of Pyongyang and said, 'The Japanese bandits still do not know the news that the Celestial troops are coming.' We also hear that Roving Commander Shen fell from his horse and hurt his foot, and is travelling by sedan chair; wanting to have the Japanese bandits send more than two hundred to meet him on the road, the Japanese commander had five Japanese go out to welcome him. When the Commander heard these words, he told us, 'I shall go ahead swiftly and instruct the generals to allow the five Japanese to come out to meet him and then to capture them alive; if we falsely say that Roving Commander Shen is about to arrive, the Japanese bandits will surely deploy troops out of the city, and with that I can strike them from ambush and win.' The Commander devises many plans, and the date of advancing the troops seems to be within three or four days; but of the various weapons loaded on carts, more than half have fallen behind. At Gasan we had the Secretary Yi Yeon-gyeong urge the dispatch of men and oxen to transport them in time, but the various offices find it hard to carry this out, and we are worried. Now at Anju we also hear that the hundred or so war carts of Roving Commander Qi have not arrived at all, and we have again sent the Secretary Yi Gwang-jeong to hurry them forward. In general, today's worry lies only in the matter of provisions, and I hear that the rice and beans stored at Sukcheon are very insufficient. We, together with the Chief Inspector and the Provisioner Yun Seung-hun, discussed it and are having grain from neighbouring towns moved in turn, and the grain that previously reached Anjeong we are giving special care to inspecting and calculating."

paragraphs.orig: ○都體察使柳成龍，馳啓曰：「天將來到肅川，有擺撥兒，自順安馳來，有急報，大將率家丁十八，與左翼都督李如栢，卽時馳去，諸軍陸續發去，未知何故。四更，巡邊使李鎰馳報云：『天將査遊擊，誘引倭二十三名，來到順安，設酒相對，仍爲捕捉。』云。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 도체찰사유성룡, 치계왈: 천장래도숙천, 유파발아, 자순안치래, 유급보, 대장솔가정십팔, 여좌익도독이여백, 즉시치거, 제군육속발거, 미지하고. 사경, 순변사이일치보운: 천장사유격, 유인왜이십삼명, 내도순안, 설주상대, 잉위포착. 운.
paragraphs.en: The Chief Inspector Yu Seong-ryong reported by express: "A Celestial general has arrived at Sukcheon. A courier came galloping from Sunan with an urgent report; the commander, leading eighteen household retainers, together with the Left Wing Commander-in-Chief Li Rubai, immediately galloped off, and the troops followed one after another. The reason is not known. At the fourth watch the Border Inspector Yi Il reported by express: 'The Celestial general Roving Commander Zha lured twenty-three Japanese to Sunan, set out wine and sat facing them, and then seized them.'"

paragraphs.orig: ○柳成龍馳啓曰：「初五日夕，李提督傳令我軍，全數聚會于平壤城外，而其中可用軍三千，今夜三更，斧山院待令云云，故時方擧行。傳聞，則明日行軍，而決戰則在於七日云。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 유성룡치계왈: 초오일석, 이제독전령아군, 전수취회우평양성외, 이기중가용군삼천, 금야삼경, 부산원대령운운, 고시방거행. 전문, 즉명일행군, 이결전즉재어칠일운.
paragraphs.en: Yu Seong-ryong reported by express: "On the evening of the fifth, Commander Li issued an order to our forces to assemble in full outside the walls of Pyongyang; among them the usable troops number three thousand, and tonight at the third watch they are to wait for orders at Busan-won Station [斧山院, 'Axe Mountain', not the port of Busan 釜山]. So this is now being carried out. It is also heard that the army marches tomorrow, and that the decisive battle will be on the seventh."
## First month, 9th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○甲子，午時，平壤捷音至。上曰：「今來報捷之人，給以銀兩，在此將官，當遣大臣、承旨問安，且於李提督處，亦當致謝問安。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 갑자, 오시, 평양첩음지. 상왈: 금래보첩지인, 급이은양, 재차장관, 당견대신, 승지문안, 차어이제독처, 역당치사문안.
paragraphs.en: On the gapja day, at noon, news of victory at Pyongyang arrived. The King said, "The man who has come to report the victory shall be given silver. As for the generals who are here, we should send senior ministers and royal secretaries to inquire after them, and to Commander Li too we should offer thanks and inquire after him."

paragraphs.orig: ○政院啓曰：「卽者，劉員外、袁主事，送家人言曰：」賴聖天子威靈，國王福氣，已摶破平壤，擒拿賊將，請面見國王。「上曰：」似當見之。但地勢狹窄，接見非便，措辭優待。「
paragraphs.reading: ○ 정원계왈: 즉자, 유원외, 원주사, 송가인언왈: 뇌성천자위령, 국왕복기, 이단파평양, 금나적장, 청면견국왕. 상왈: 사당견지. 단지세협착, 접견비편, 조사우대.
paragraphs.en: The Royal Secretariat reported: "Just now Supernumerary Liu and Secretary Yuan sent household servants to say, 'Thanks to the might of the Holy Son of Heaven and the blessed vapour of the King, Pyongyang has been smashed and the enemy commanders seized. We ask to see the King in person.'" The King said, "It seems proper to see them. But the ground is cramped and receiving them would be inconvenient; answer with courteous words."

paragraphs.orig: ○大臣二品以上兩司長官啓曰：「聞平壤捷音，不知所達。」上曰：「諸卿之力，皇恩罔極，不知所諭。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 대신이품이상양사장관계왈: 문평양첩음, 부지소달. 상왈: 제경지력, 황은망극, 부지소유.
paragraphs.en: The senior ministers of the second rank and above and the heads of the two offices reported: "We have heard the news of victory at Pyongyang and do not know how to convey it." The King said, "It is through your strength. The imperial grace is boundless; I cannot express it."

paragraphs.orig: ○上敎政院曰：「宋侍郞處，亦當致謝，議啓。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 상교정원왈: 송시랑처, 역당치사, 의계.
paragraphs.en: The King instructed the Royal Secretariat: "We should also express our thanks to Vice-Minister Song; deliberate and report."

paragraphs.orig: ○尹根壽來啓曰：「聞初八日，李提督進戰于箕城，倭將使張大膳請曰：『願暫退天兵，奉表納貢于福建。』提督答曰：『爾等欲降，則二千出城外，聽我命可也。爾等，何敢出退天兵之說也？退兵，則決不可從。』張大膳曰：『然則老爺自爲之。』李提督戰時，倭將亦督戰于西門。天兵進戰，斬殺無數，祖總兵、李寧領我軍，入南門，天兵放三穴鳥銃，倭軍盡斃，只餘三四百盡入松林間。李如松、汝梅等，進迫大同門，倭軍中，多發片箭，中者甚多，天將曰：『爾國之人甚惡』云云。倭死者滿城，而李提督不令斬一級云。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 윤근수래계왈: 문초팔일, 이제독진전우기성, 왜장사장대선청왈: 원잠퇴천병, 봉표납공우복건. 제독답왈: 이등욕항, 즉이천출성외, 청아명가야. 이등, 하감출퇴천병지설야? 퇴병, 즉결불가종. 장대선왈: 연즉노야자위지. 이제독전시, 왜장역독전우서문. 천병진전, 참살무수, 조총병, 이녕령아군, 입남문, 천병방삼혈조총, 왜군진폐, 지여삼사백진입송림간. 이여송, 여매등, 진박대동문, 왜군중, 다발편전, 중자심다, 천장왈: 이국지인심악운운. 왜사자만성, 이이제독불령참일급운.
paragraphs.en: Yun Geun-su came and reported: "I hear that on the eighth Commander Li advanced and fought at Giseong [Pyongyang]. The Japanese general sent Zhang Daxian to request, 'We beg you to withdraw the Celestial troops for a while; we will present a memorial and offer tribute at Fujian.' The Commander answered, 'If you wish to surrender, send two thousand men outside the city and obey my orders. How dare you speak of withdrawing the Celestial troops? To withdraw the troops is absolutely impossible.' Zhang Daxian said, 'Then do it yourself, Sir.' While Commander Li was fighting, the Japanese general also supervised the fighting at the west gate. The Celestial troops advanced and fought and killed countless men; Regional Commander Zu and Li Ning [a Ming officer; the text is ambiguous] led our troops into the south gate; the Celestial troops fired their three-barrelled arquebuses, and the Japanese were all felled, leaving only three or four hundred, all of whom entered the pine woods. Li Rusong and Rumei and others pressed on to the Daedong Gate; from among the Japanese troops many dart-arrows were shot, and very many were hit. The Celestial generals said, 'The people of your country are most vicious,' and so on. The Japanese dead filled the city, but Commander Li did not allow a single head to be taken."

paragraphs.orig: ○上敎政院曰：「平壤之賊，已爲掃蕩，歸路整齊，舟師水戰掩擊事，兩南水使處，遣宣傳官，卽爲下諭。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 상교정원왈: 평양지적, 이위소탕, 귀로정제, 주사수전엄격사, 양남수사처, 견선전관, 즉위하유.
paragraphs.en: The King instructed the Royal Secretariat: "The enemy at Pyongyang has been swept away. As to making ready the line of their return and the naval ambush attack, send royal messengers to the naval commanders of the two southern provinces and instruct them at once."

paragraphs.orig: ○上曰：「天將在一城之中，皇恩罔極，欲躬造以謝。雖犯夜，何關？問于大臣以啓。」大臣啓曰：「極當。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 상왈: 천장재일성지중, 황은망극, 욕궁조이사. 수범야, 하관? 문우대신이계. 대신계왈: 극당.
paragraphs.en: The King said, "The Celestial generals are within one city; the imperial grace is boundless, and I wish to go in person to thank them. Even if it violates the curfew, what does it matter? Ask the ministers and report." The ministers reported, "It is entirely proper."

paragraphs.orig: ○上出御龍灣館，接見劉員外、袁主事。上曰：「賴皇上威靈，已勦箕城之賊，恢復舊疆，指日可待，請行謝拜。」兩人曰：「此是皇上之恩，俺不敢私受。」上曰：「請拜謝皇恩。」上設席向北，行五拜禮訖，與兩人再拜。兩人曰：「請賀拜。」上辭曰：「惶恐。」兩人固請，上曰：「不敢當。」兩人曰：「義智、行長，已在圍中，便可砲殺。此非常之喜也。」上曰：「皇恩罔極。又兩大人，贊畫軍謀，致此大功，不勝感激。」兩人答曰：「此實賴國王福德，俺何力之有？」仍行茶禮。劉員外曰：「已克平壤，本國人有投入賊中者，若自來，則饒而勿罪可也。其中同惡向導者外，自來者，何必罪之？」袁主事曰：「事定後，若以一切之法，深治投入之人，則不可也。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 상출어용만관, 접견유원외, 원주사. 상왈: 뇌황상위령, 이초기성지적, 회복구강, 지일가대, 청행사배. 양인왈: 차시황상지은, 엄불감사수. 상왈: 청배사황은. 상설석향북, 행오배례흘, 여양인재배. 양인왈: 청하배. 상사왈: 황공. 양인고청, 상왈: 불감당. 양인왈: 의지, 행장, 이재위중, 편가포살. 차비상지희야. 상왈: 황은망극. 우양대인, 찬화군모, 치차대공, 불승감격. 양인답왈: 차실뢰국왕복덕, 엄하력지유? 잉행다례. 유원외왈: 이극평양, 본국인유투입적중자, 약자래, 즉요이물죄가야. 기중동악향도자외, 자래자, 하필죄지? 원주사왈: 사정후, 약이일체지법, 심치투입지인, 즉불가야.
paragraphs.en: The King went out to Yongman Lodge and received Supernumerary Liu and Secretary Yuan. The King said, "Thanks to the Emperor's might, the bandits at Giseong [Pyongyang] have already been destroyed, and recovery of our old territory is a matter of days. I ask to perform the rite of thanks." The two men said, "This is the Emperor's grace; we dare not accept it for ourselves." The King said, "I ask to bow in thanks for the imperial grace." The King had a mat spread facing north and performed the five bows; when it was finished he bowed twice to the two men. The two men said, "We ask to receive your congratulatory bow." The King declined, saying, "I am overawed." The two pressed him firmly. The King said, "I dare not accept it." The two men said, "Yoshitoshi and Yukinaga are already within the encirclement, and can be shelled to death. This is an extraordinary joy." The King said, "The imperial grace is boundless. And you two Excellencies, aiding with plans for the campaign, have brought about this great achievement; I cannot bear my gratitude." The two men answered, "This truly depends on the King's blessed virtue; what strength have we had?" Then they performed the tea ceremony. Supernumerary Liu said, "Now that Pyongyang has been conquered, if people of your country who went over to the enemy come of their own accord, they may be spared and not punished. Apart from those who joined in evil as guides, why must those who come of their own accord be punished?" Secretary Yuan said, "After matters are settled, if one were to punish deeply, by uniform law, those who went over to the enemy, that would not be right."

paragraphs.orig: ○司諫院啓曰：「西賊，今已勦滅。天聲所曁，自有破竹之勢，京城恢復，指日可待。第念北賊踰嶺之計，難保其必無，要害諸處，芻糧未備。該司必已措處，而自京城到釜山，一路糧餉告竭。若天兵乘勝直下，措辦無策，兩湖之穀，不可不急速輸運，以爲急時之用。且江原一道，比他道稍完，若差遣募栗官，趁時收聚，則可及鐵嶺一路緩急之用。請令該司，斯速擧行。」上從之。
paragraphs.reading: ○ 사간원계왈: 서적, 금이초멸. 천성소기, 자유파죽지세, 경성회복, 지일가대. 제념북적유령지계, 난보기필무, 요해제처, 추량미비. 해사필이조처, 이자경성도부산, 일로량향고갈. 약천병승승직하, 조판무책, 양호지곡, 불가불급속수운, 이위급시지용. 차강원일도, 비타도초완, 약차견모율관, 진시수취, 즉가급철령일로완급지용. 청령해사, 사속거행. 상종지.
paragraphs.en: The Office of Remonstrators reported: "The western bandits have now been destroyed. Wherever the Celestial voice reaches there is a bamboo-splitting momentum, and the recovery of the capital is a matter of days. But we consider that the northern bandits' plan to cross the ridge cannot be guaranteed not to occur, and at the strategic points fodder and provisions are not yet prepared. The office concerned must have made arrangements, but from the capital to Busan, the provisions along the whole road have run out. If the Celestial troops press on in victory, we shall have no means to provide for them; the grain of the two Ho provinces (Honam and Hoseo) must be transported quickly for urgent use. Moreover, Gangwon Province alone is somewhat more intact than the other provinces; if officials are sent to collect grain by contribution at the right time, we can meet the urgent needs of the Cheollyeong road. We ask that the office concerned act swiftly." The King followed.

paragraphs.orig: ○良人柳億等，夜入賊中，陪奉仁、明兩大王位版而來，備邊司啓請軍職除授，或免賤論賞。
paragraphs.reading: ○ 양인유억등, 야입적중, 배봉인, 명양대왕위판이래, 비변사계청군직제수, 혹면천론상.
paragraphs.en: Commoners Yu Eok and others went into the enemy's midst at night and brought back the spirit tablets of the two great kings 'In' and 'Myeong' [presumably Injong and Myeongjong]. The Border Defence Council petitioned for the conferral of military posts on them, or for release from base status and the granting of rewards.

paragraphs.orig: ○都體察使柳成龍馳啓曰：「初八日已時，唐將已爲接戰，四面攻城，放砲之聲，如雷如震。天兵破七星門而入，時方厮殺，平壤似已收復，不勝喜幸之至，謹先馳啓。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 도체찰사유성룡치계왈: 초팔일이시, 당장이위접전, 사면공성, 방포지성, 여뢰여진. 천병파칠성문이입, 시방시살, 평양사이수복, 불승희행지지, 근선치계.
paragraphs.en: The Chief Inspector Yu Seong-ryong reported by express: "At the hour of the snake (9-11 a.m.) on the eighth, the Tang [i.e. Chinese] generals had already engaged the enemy, attacking the city on all four sides; the sound of the cannon was like thunder, like quaking. The Celestial troops broke through the Chilseong Gate and entered, and are now in hand-to-hand slaughter. Pyongyang seems already to have been retaken; I cannot contain my joy and hasten to report first."
## Eleventh month, 7th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○備邊司啓曰：「設險事，經略累次移咨，故節次遣工曹等官，往委料理。雖其人力殫竭，難可遽議設築，而如有可設之處，則亦當觀勢隨便，以爲防備之計。經略咨文，則只擧大丘、仁同矣，如右道三嘉山城，最係要害。邑民亦皆願築，此亦更爲知委，使之有成。此外高靈山城、陜川冶鑪山城、伽倻山、金山山城、安陰等處山城，皆爲絶險，而左道公山，正當大丘、淸道之會，地勢極險，故前年倭賊，充斥於山下，而避亂之人，多在絶頂，賊兵終不得上，民多賴此全活，此亦似當幷爲料理。但其處人民，飢餓流離，驅之於畚築之役，雖出於生道，而人心怨咨，似或難成。如令義僧將弘靖，率其軍若干，備一月糧，漸次修築，而助以本處之民，則不無有成之理。但遠處之事，難以遙度。大臣旣已下去，自當觀勢便否，而處置得宜。然以此意下書，察其道內人情及形勢緩急，不計日時遲速，從容處之何如？」答曰：「依啓。」
paragraphs.reading: ○ 비변사계왈: 설험사, 경략누차이자, 고절차견공조등관, 왕위요리. 수기인력탄갈, 난가거의설축, 이여유가설지처, 즉역당관세수편, 이위방비지계. 경략자문, 즉지거대구, 인동의, 여우도삼가산성, 최계요해. 읍민역개원축, 차역갱위지위, 사지유성. 차외고령산성, 합천야로산성, 가야산, 금산산성, 안음등처산성, 개위절험, 이좌도공산, 정당대구, 청도지회, 지세극험, 고전년왜적, 충척어산하, 이피란지인, 다재절정, 적병종부득상, 민다뢰차전활, 차역사당병위요리. 단기처인민, 기아유리, 구지어분축지역, 수출어생도, 이인심원자, 사혹난성. 여령의승장홍정, 솔기군약간, 비일월량, 점차수축, 이조이본처지민, 즉불무유성지리. 단원처지사, 난이요탁. 대신기이하거, 자당관세편부, 이처치득의. 연이차의하서, 찰기도내인정급형세완급, 불계일시지속, 종용처지하여? 답왈: 의계.
paragraphs.en: The Border Defence Council reported: "On the matter of building defences, the Military Commissioner has repeatedly sent notes, so we have sent officials of the Board of Works and others in sequence to oversee it. Although manpower is exhausted and it is hard to deliberate building at once, if there are places where building is possible, we should observe the lie of the land and, accordingly, make plans for defence. The Commissioner's note mentions only Daegu and Indong; but, for example, the Samga mountain fortress in the right circuit is the most strategic; the people of the town all wish to build it, and this too should again be made known to them so that it is completed. Besides these, the mountain fortresses of Goryeong, Hapcheon's Yarosan, Gayasan, Geumsan, Aneum and other places are all extremely precipitous; and in the left circuit Gongsan stands exactly where Daegu and Cheongdo meet and its terrain is extremely steep. In the previous year the Japanese bandits swarmed at the foot of the mountain, while refugees were mostly at the summit, and the enemy troops could never climb up; many people were saved by this. That too ought to be dealt with together. But the people of that area are starving and drifting; to drive them to the labour of baskets and ramming, though it is for a path of survival, resentment may make it hard to accomplish. If the righteous monk-commander Hongjeong were to lead some of his troops with a month's provisions and build gradually, assisted by the local people, then there would be reason to expect completion. But matters at a distance are hard to judge from afar. The ministers have already gone down, and will naturally judge the situation and act appropriately. Yet we propose sending this intention to the circuit in writing, examining the feelings of the people within the circuit and the urgency of conditions, and handling it calmly without regard to whether it takes days or longer; what do you think?" The reply: "As proposed."
## Intercalary eleventh month, 8th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: (○)備邊司啓曰：「伏見經略咨文，聖旨嚴切，雖出於責成之意，極爲未安。今此天使回還後，似當別爲一奏，陳情乞恩，請令承文院，預爲磨鍊。」答曰：「依啓。且經略，每以四件事嚴責，至於題奏，事將不測。今於天使前，別爲揭帖，明辨其意。且於兵部，小邦殘破力綿，只有孑遺殘民，築城等事，雖欲極力措置，勢所難能之意，善辭移咨，以爲後日張本，如何？議啓。」
paragraphs.reading: (○ )비변사계왈: 복견경략자문, 성지엄절, 수출어책성지의, 극위미안. 금차천사회환후, 사당별위일주, 진정걸은, 청령승문원, 예위마련. 답왈: 의계. 차경략, 매이사건사엄책, 지어제주, 사장불측. 금어천사전, 별위게첩, 명변기의. 차어병부, 소방잔파력면, 지유혈유잔민, 축성등사, 수욕극력조치, 세소난능지의, 선사이자, 이위후일장본, 여하? 의계.
paragraphs.en: (○) The Border Defence Council reported: "Having read the Military Commissioner's note, the imperial decree is severe; although it comes from the intention of demanding results, it is extremely uneasy. After this Celestial envoy has returned, it seems that we should submit a separate memorial stating our circumstances and begging mercy; we request that the Office of Diplomatic Documents prepare it in advance." The reply: "As proposed. Also, the Commissioner constantly reproaches us severely on four items, and as for the matter of memorials, events may become unpredictable. Now, before the Celestial envoy, let us separately compose a statement to explain our meaning clearly. And to the Ministry of War, in well-chosen words, send a note saying that our small country is shattered and weak, that only a remnant of survivors is left, and that although we would like to exert every effort in matters such as wall-building, circumstances make it impossible, so as to serve as groundwork for later; what do you think? Deliberate and report."

paragraphs.orig: ○備邊司啓曰：「近日，沿途各處，盜賊興行，至於殺掠天兵，奪取公文，極爲駭愕。非但一處，如順安唐人致死，亦甚可疑，而前日竹山，屯聚山頭，追逐擺撥兒等事，相繼不絶。若不痛加緝獲，以絶其端，則將來之變，必有甚於今日。地方守令，雖當推治，而觀察使、兵使，亦宜常川撿勑，俾無竊發之患，乃其職也。今宋侍郞，以徐鋤頭之事，至於移咨。此亦不無造生釁端之慮。黃海監司、兵使推考，今後盜賊瞭察等事，另爲申勑之意，竝入於回咨中。」上從之。
paragraphs.reading: ○ 비변사계왈: 근일, 연도각처, 도적흥행, 지어살략천병, 탈취공문, 극위해악. 비단일처, 여순안당인치사, 역심가의, 이전일죽산, 둔취산두, 추축파발아등사, 상계부절. 약불통가집획, 이절기단, 즉장래지변, 필유심어금일. 지방수령, 수당추치, 이관찰사, 병사, 역의상천검칙, 비무절발지환, 내기직야. 금송시랑, 이서서두지사, 지어이자. 차역불무조생흔단지려. 황해감사, 병사추고, 금후도적료찰등사, 영위신칙지의, 병입어회자중. 상종지.
paragraphs.en: The Border Defence Council reported: "Recently, along the road, brigands have arisen in many places, to the point of killing and plundering Celestial troops and seizing official documents; this is extremely shocking. It is not in one place only; the death of a Tang man at Sunan, for example, is also very suspicious, and previously at Juksan people gathered on the mountain heights and chased courier messengers, one case after another without end. If we do not vigorously arrest them to cut off the source, the calamity to come will surely be greater than today's. The local magistrates should of course be investigated, but the governors and military commanders ought also to keep inspecting and warning, so that there are no stealthy outbreaks; that is their duty. Now Vice-Minister Song, over the affair of Xu Chutou, has even sent a note. This too may well create a cause of friction. Let the governor and the military commander of Hwanghae be questioned, and let the instruction to give special warnings from now on on the matter of watching for brigands be included in the reply note." The King followed.
## Intercalary eleventh month, 9th day (lunar)

paragraphs.orig: ○左議政尹斗壽等馳啓曰：「本月二十四日，摠兵令臣等喫茶，仍俾左右言：『今日，閣老、元帥、尙書、布政、侍郞，皆在於此，與國王面議，一般也。今與賊相守，欲戰不戰，欲和不和，遷延日久，師老糧盡。今計和親是耶？勦滅是耶？』臣等答曰：『自古講和成事者無。進兵勦殺，是我國所望。』摠兵喜曰：『當初經略、提督，與倭講和時，封貢則有言，而和親兩字，今始聞。此是沈家潛約之言。宋爺稍聞此言，前欲綑打，而解送摠府，朝廷全不知之。朝廷若知則，宋爺亦不免死』云。本國兵糧、中朝請兵事，令臣等急速詳議回話，臣等問：『限何日月，催儧兵糧乎？」摠兵答曰：『爲將，隨天時、地利、人和而處之，不可預期。然正、二月爲限擧事。國王、群臣，下至士庶，皆有不共戴天之讎，鼓動義氣，以此從事，事必成矣。賊殺我千、把摠四人，不勝忿忿。勦賊之日，剮倭心肝，臠而食之。』因張目發怒，良久而後已。臣等竊念，慶尙道一萬五千兵、兩湖一萬六百、平安一千、黃海六百、京畿、江原各四百抄發，各持一月糧，臨時入送事，都元帥已爲出令，而臣等時方料理措處矣。「
paragraphs.reading: ○ 좌의정윤두수등치계왈: 본월이십사일, 총병령신등끽다, 잉비좌우언: 금일, 각로, 원수, 상서, 포정, 시랑, 개재어차, 여국왕면의, 일반야. 금여적상수, 욕전부전, 욕화불화, 천연일구, 사로량진. 금계화친시야? 초멸시야? 신등답왈: 자고강화성사자무. 진병초살, 시아국소망. 총병희왈: 당초경략, 제독, 여왜강화시, 봉공즉유언, 이화친양자, 금시문. 차시심가잠약지언. 송야초문차언, 전욕곤타, 이해송총부, 조정전부지지. 조정약지즉, 송야역불면사운. 본국병량, 중조청병사, 영신등급속상의회화, 신등문: 한하일월, 최찬병량호? 총병답왈: 위장, 수천시, 지리, 인화이처지, 불가예기. 연정, 이월위한거사. 국왕, 군신, 하지사서, 개유불공대천지수, 고동의기, 이차종사, 사필성의. 적살아천, 파총사인, 불승분분. 초적지일, 과왜심간, 연이식지. 인장목발로, 양구이후이. 신등절념, 경상도일만오천병, 양호일만육백, 평안일천, 황해륙백, 경기, 강원각사백초발, 각지일월량, 임시입송사, 도원수이위출령, 이신등시방요리조처의.
paragraphs.en: The Left State Councillor Yun Du-su and others reported by express: "On the twenty-fourth of this month [the entry is dated in the intercalary month, so the 11th month is probably meant], the Regional Commander had us drink tea and then had his attendants say, 'Today the Grand Secretary, the Marshal, the Minister, the Provincial Administration Commissioner and the Vice-Minister are all here; discussing with the King face to face is the same. Now we are facing the bandits in a stand-off, wanting to fight yet not fighting, wanting peace yet not making peace, delaying for many days, the army worn and the provisions exhausted. Now do you reckon that friendly relations are right, or annihilation?' We answered, 'From of old no one has accomplished anything by making peace. To advance and annihilate them is what our country hopes.' The Regional Commander was pleased and said, 'At the beginning, when Commissioner Song and Commander Li were negotiating peace with the Japanese, there was talk of investiture and tribute, but the two words "friendly relations" I hear only now. This is the secret agreement of Shen's house. When Master Song heard something of these words, he earlier wanted to have him bound and beaten, and sent him under escort to the General's office; the court knows nothing of this at all. If the court knew, Master Song too would not escape death.' He told us to deliberate swiftly on our country's military provisions and on the request to the Middle Court for troops, and to give him an answer. We asked, 'By what date should the troops and provisions be urgently gathered?' The Regional Commander answered, 'A general acts according to the timing of heaven, the advantage of terrain and the harmony of men; one cannot set a date in advance. But let the first and second months be the limit for taking action. The King, the officials, and down to the common people all have an enemy with whom they cannot share the same heaven; stir up righteous spirit and act on it, and the matter will surely succeed. The bandits have killed four of my thousand-commanders and company-commanders, and I am boiling with rage. On the day we annihilate the bandits I will slice out the Japanese hearts and livers, cut them up and eat them.' Then he glared and raged, and it was a long time before he stopped. We privately consider that the troops to be drafted are: from Gyeongsang Province fifteen thousand, from the two Ho provinces (Honam and Hoseo) ten thousand six hundred, from Pyongan one thousand, from Hwanghae six hundred, and four hundred each from Gyeonggi and Gangwon, each carrying a month's provisions, to be sent in at the time. The Commander-in-Chief has already issued the order, and we are now arranging and handling it."

paragraphs.orig: ○領議政柳成龍啓曰：「臣昨日伏見經略咨文，爲之達夜不寐。國事日益危迫，討賊之外，又有此難處之事，實如聖敎，將有不測之虞，不勝痛悶。且兵部題本中：『勿許本國再爲請援，以絶後日奏聞之路。』經略必執此爲辭，通行於巡按遼東衙門，不許通奏，則將何以處之？大抵初來，不爲卽行分付，展轉相激，以至於此。大臣雖已下去，而三曹判書，猶在此處，天使若問何故尙不進去，則對之極難。臣意李恒福、金命元，不可不急急下去。若是則恒福不必遞兵曹，而遠接之任，旣以鄭琢代之，則恒福不必進見而南下，則恐有對答之路。且今此天使接對措辭之間，所係非輕，臣略草前後賊情始末及近日奉行諸件之事，以擬隨問對答，或以此爲咨文及奏文，痛陳賊勢，而倉卒多有斤正處。臣今將出去，令承文院，繕寫投進，以備聖覽裁定。」答曰：「此言當則當矣，李恒福必已爲遠接使，所任如何？三曹判書，何以不去乎，問之則，以策應軍務事未去。姑以副官下送事，未可對答乎？」回啓曰：「李恒福若已進見於天使，則如此處置亦難。今當急急下書于恒福，問其進見與否，然後處之爲當。三曹判書，不爲下去事，依上敎，對答極當。但，初則但是經略分付，今旣題奉聖旨，似不得不去。天使入來後，以此答之而發送，亦無妨。」答曰：「下書事，依啓。三曹判書，不得不去，下送爲當。」

paragraphs.en: The Chief State Councillor Yu Seong-ryong reported: "Yesterday I read the Military Commissioner's note and did not sleep all night. State affairs grow daily more critical; besides punishing the bandits, there is this difficult matter, truly as Your Majesty's instruction says, with unforeseeable dangers; I cannot bear the distress. Moreover, the Ministry of War's memorial says, 'Do not allow the country to request relief again, so as to cut off the path of reporting to the throne in the future.' The Commissioner is bound to take this as his argument and circulate it to the Inspector's office of Liaodong to forbid any communication of memorials; and then how shall we deal with it? In general, when he first came, no immediate instruction was given; one thing provoked another, until it came to this. The ministers have already gone down, but the ministers of the three Boards are still here; if the Celestial envoy asks why they have not yet gone forward, it will be extremely hard to answer. In my view Yi Hang-bok and Kim Myeong-won must be sent down urgently. If so, Hang-bok need not be replaced as Minister of War, and since the duty of distant reception has been handed to Jeong Tak, Hang-bok need not go to an audience but go south, and then there may be a way to answer. Moreover, in the present reception of and dealing with the Celestial envoy, the wording of our replies is of no small weight. I have roughly drafted the sequence of the enemy's circumstances and the matters recently carried out, to be used for answers to questions; perhaps it can be made into a note or a memorial to state the enemy's momentum vigorously, but in haste there are many places that need correcting. Now I am about to go out and shall have the Office of Diplomatic Documents make a fair copy and submit it for Your Majesty's decision." The reply: "These words are proper, but Yi Hang-bok must already be the reception envoy; what of his duty? Why have the ministers of the three Boards not gone? When I asked, they said they had not gone because of the business of responding to military affairs. For now, send them down as deputy officers: can we not answer in that way?" The reply report: "If Hang-bok has already been received by the Celestial envoy, this arrangement too would be difficult. Now we should send a letter urgently to Hang-bok to ask whether he has had the audience or not, and then act accordingly. As for the ministers of the three Boards not going down, to answer as your instruction says is entirely proper. But at first it was only the Commissioner's order, and now that it has been noted in the imperial decree, it seems we cannot but go. After the Celestial envoy comes in, we can answer him in this way and send them off without harm." The reply: "As to sending the letter, as proposed. The ministers of the three Boards cannot but go; it is right to send them down."
